title: NN/g, “Neobrutalism: Definition and Best Practices”
lede: A usability firm’s definition of the style, with accessibility guidance.
summary: Nielsen Norman Group’s 2025 definition: high contrast, blocky layout, bold color, thick borders.

evidence.note: Article text read on 2026-09-25. Byline and date (11 April 2025) are on the page.

styles.note: An authoritative UX source that defines the style under both spellings and lists its traits.

context: Definition: “Neobrutalism (or neubrutalism), an evolution of traditional brutalism, is a visual-design trend defined by high contrast, blocky layouts, bold colors, thick borders, and ‘unpolished’ elements.”
It separates the two: brutalist sites “might use plain HTML elements and limited color palettes” (example: Drudge Report), while neobrutalist designs “are likely to be more colorful and orderly”.

On shadows: “solid, single-color shadows (e.g., a black drop shadow offset by 4px)”. Examples include Gumroad, Figma, 99percentoffsale.com, byooooob.com, cyanbanister.com, dodonut.com, and bieffeforniture.it.
Best practices: meet contrast ratios, limit the palette to 2 or 3 bold colors, pair chunky headings with neutral body fonts, and pad dense shapes with 24 to 32 px.
interpretation: Useful for attestation of the name and for the brutalism versus neobrutalism distinction. Some of its examples lean retro or brutalist rather than outline-and-shadow, so each needs a capture.
